description.value: The study examined reflection impulsivity in binge drinkers and healthy volunteers using the beads task and Information Sampling Task, and investigated volumetric brain correlates with voxel-based morphometry.

value: We hypothesized that binge drinkers would have impairments in both forms of decisional impulsivity.
We focused on the aforementioned regions hypothesizing a relationship between greater impulsivity and decreases in brain volume in these regions.

definition.value: The number of beads drawn in the beads task was positively correlated with grey matter volume.

spans.text: The number of beads drawn in the beads task (lower impulsivity) was positively correlated with greater volume in the left (L) cerebellum (−39 −84 −21, cluster size = 217, Z = 4.15), L DLPFC (−22 45 28, cluster size = 271, Z = 3.87), L inferior parietal cortex (−45 −44 30, cluster size = 98, Z = 3.75) and right (R) thalamus (17 −26 6, cluster size = 50, Z = 3.28) (Fig.  1 ).

value: Greater impulsivity as indexed by lower evidence accumulation in the beads task was associated with smaller L DLPFC and L inferior parietal volumes.

model_settings.value: Grey matter volumes were analysed using voxel-wise covariate analyses, with proportional scaling for total intracranial volume; age and gender were covariates of no interest, and AUDIT score was included in a separate analysis. Cluster-extent correction used 19 voxels at P < 0.001 whole-brain uncorrected, corrected to P < 0.05.

description.value: Participants viewed sequentially presented coloured beads drawn from one of two jars and decided which jar they came from.

instructions.value: Subjects were shown two jars with opposite ratios of red and blue beads and were told that beads from one jar would be presented one at a time. They had to infer which jar the beads came from, could view as many beads as desired up to a maximum of 20, and then commit to a decision.
